s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of neurological deficits with tumefactive brain lesion
salient_findings: Subacute onset of expressive aphasia and right-sided hemiparesis
Large T2-hyperintense, tumefactive lesion in the left prefrontal white matter
key_facts: 23-year history of presumed multiple sclerosis
Four episodes of optic neuritis since 1989
Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis in 1995
Persistently negative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) oligoclonal bands
Unremarkable brain MRI scans prior to 2012
Normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
Normal vital signs
Expressive language impairment and 3/5 strength in the right arm and leg
CSF analysis was unremarkable with no evidence of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis
No oligoclonal bands in CSF
Normal cell count in CSF
No signs of vasculitis on time-of-flight MR angiography
No clinical or serological evidence for connective tissue diseases
Serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre was 1:1000 by cell-based assay

shortlist.label: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder
shortlist.why_kept: High serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre and subacute onset of neurological deficits with tumefactive brain lesion

shortlist.label: Tumefactive multiple sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of presumed multiple sclerosis and presence of tumefactive brain lesion

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of tumefactive brain lesion and unremarkable CSF analysis

shortlist.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of neurological deficits and presence of tumefactive brain lesion

shortlist.label: Multiple sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: 23-year history of presumed multiple sclerosis and presence of new neurological deficits

raw.rationale: The patient's history of longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, optic neuritis, and the presence of a high serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre are characteristic of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, which better explains the clinical presentation than multiple sclerosis, especially given the persistently negative CSF oligoclonal bands and the nature of the lesions.

rejected.label: Tumefactive multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: The lack of oligoclonal bands in CSF and the presence of aquaporin-4 antibodies are not typical for tumefactive multiple sclerosis.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not strongly suggest a lymphoma, and CSF analysis did not indicate the presence of lymphoma cells.

rejected.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: The patient's history of recurrent episodes of optic neuritis and myelitis over many years does not fit the monophasic nature of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis.

rejected.label: Multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: The presence of aquaporin-4 antibodies and the characteristics of the lesions are more indicative of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder than multiple sclerosis, especially given the atypical features for MS such as negative oligoclonal bands and the specific type of lesions.
